correctness.rationale: The change u=de x, θ=dy mod 2π preserves the angular increment. A quotient fixed point has u=2πj=A/(1−k cos θ)>0, so j is positive and cos θ=(1−r_j)/k completely gives existence and multiplicity. The trace is 2−r_j, and the two determinants are 1−r_j±S_j; on the positive-sine branch the Schur quantities are S_j, 4−2r_j+S_j, and r_j−S_j. The middle one is positive since r_j<2. The negative-sine characteristic polynomial is negative at 1, proving a real multiplier >1. The phase-merger endpoints have eigenvalue 1, and S_j=r_j in the interior gives a unit complex pair; no nonlinear classification at those boundaries is needed. In the explicit family r_m=1+t and r_{m+1}=1−t. The larger of the ratios S_j/r_j has square π²/m² times (1/50+1/[10000(m+1)²]), strictly below one. The integer band A/[2π(1+k)]≤j≤A/[2π(1−k)] lies strictly between m−1 and m+2 and contains m and m+1 in its interior; the strict margins persist locally. A hyperbolic sink gives summable increments u_n−2πj after the orbit reaches its local neighborhood, hence the stated lift with an orbit-dependent constant and open disjoint basins. The bound |u_{n+1}|≤A+k|u_n| gives liminf u_n≥A(1−2k)/(1−k)>0 at the explicit k_m, proving global eventual upward drift without claiming a global limiting speed. Independent exact band and Schur-margin tests at seven indices, with supplementary direct eigenvalue checks, agree. Replay: python /workspace/branches/independent_replay.py 3.
residual_risks: Finite diagnostics do not classify all indices by themselves. The result concerns hyperbolic one-step quotient sinks; no claim about higher periods or nonlinear behavior on neutral boundaries. The assertion k_m→0 permits A and the winding indices to vary.
